title: [replay r7] feat(desktop): Export screen with its own rail entry (replaces Prepare)
body:
> **Replay of [niway-dev/kaipu-record#467](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/467), run 7** for the code-review benchmark. Same base and head commits as the round-1 replay (a second branch name on the same commit, so the reviewer sees a fresh pull request). Never merged. Method: [wachiman/docs/benchmark](https://github.com/niway-dev/wachiman/tree/main/docs/benchmark).

---

## What

Replaces the Prepare screen with **Export**, following the Claude Design file "Kaipu Export v3", section 3 "EXPORT · ITS OWN SCREEN".

- **Rail.** A new **EXPORT** entry (upload icon) directly under EDITOR. Its badge (the copy being exported now plus finished copies not seen yet) moves there from LIBRARY.
- **Routes.** `/export/:assetId` and `/export`. Old `/prepare/:assetId` and `/prepare` URLs redirect there with the query kept (`?to=`). `preparePath()` / `prepareNewPath()` keep their names and signatures and now return Export URLs, so sibling branches that call them land on Export unchanged.
- **Header (fixed).** A 96×54 thumbnail, the title (ellipsis), ORIGINAL, and the real "0:17 · 1920 × 1050 · 4.6 MB · copies are made from this file; it never changes". **Change video** lists the Library's originals.
- **Stage.** Nothing picked: the fox and "Where is it going?". A destination picked: its logo, "For …" and one sentence. Upload destinations show **Upload size** (YouTube 1440p / 4K with real estimates; TikTok · Reels and LinkedIn · Feeds show their single canvas plus Fill / Fit) and the before/after text crops. Light destinations show the size bar; GitHub's is drawn against the free 10 MB limit (`githubPlans().free`). Then the pink Export button with ↵.
- **Destination row (fixed).** "WHERE IS IT GOING?" with the amber/teal legend, and seven equal cards. The row scrolls sideways on its own when the cards don't fit; the page never scrolls. ←/→ move the selection; Enter exports.
- **No video.** The "Export" header, a dashed drop zone with **Pick from Library** and **Browse files…**, and **Recent exports** (the copy in progress with its percentage, then the newest finished copies, three in all). It reuses `useImportVideos` and the window-wide drop handling from #459.
- **Library.** The drop strip, "Prepare a video" and "Import a video" are gone, and the Library no longer takes window drops. Export is the way in for outside videos.

The preset resolution, estimates, `usePrepareCopy`, `usePrepareImport` and the export runner are reused unchanged. The screen is restyled, not rewritten.

## Why

This addresses the owner's feedback on Prepare:
1. You couldn't tell which video you were preparing.
2. The video info has to stay fixed while the destination list scrolls on its own.
3. The Library had too many jobs.

## Decisions to review

- **Email is a destination of its own** that uses the same Balanced preset as Slack · Discord. The design has seven cards and there are only six presets. A Balanced copy therefore shows "Ready" on both cards, and `destinationOfPreset("balanced")` still returns `chat`.
- **The progress and ready cards say "your export" for an Email copy.** Their ICU `select` has no `email` branch, and those strings belong to the toasts branch.
- **The "About N minutes." line is left out.** The app has no measured encode-time estimate yet, so the line only says the export runs in the background.
- **Export stays on screen after it starts.** Prepare went back to the recording. Now the progress card shows the export, and another destination is one click away.
- **Code layout.** The page lives in `pages/export/` and its strings in a new `export` i18n namespace. The shared logic stays in `features/prepare/`, and the destination vocabulary the other screens use stays under `prepare`. This keeps merges with the sibling branches (recording page, post-recording card, Library cards, toasts) conflict-free. The only sibling-owned file touched is `library-detail-page.test.tsx`, whose expected path changes from `/prepare/…` to `/export/…`.
- **Deletions.** `ImportDropZone` is deleted, since the Library was its only user. Its `useFileDrop` coverage moved to `use-file-drop.test.tsx`.

## Stack

Base: `feature/niw2-587-prepare-drop-zone` (#459), the top of the Prepare stack (#436 ← #448 ← #458 ← #455 ← #457 ← #456 ← #459). No Linear ticket, because the workspace hit its issue limit. The backlog page is `backlog/export-screen`.

## Verification

`bun run verify` passes: lint, format, build, types, and every test suite (kaipu-record: 317 files, 3090 tests). The app was **not** run in Electron.

## How to test it yourself

1. Check out this branch, then run `bun install` and `bun run dev`.
2. Look at the rail. **EXPORT** (upload icon) sits right under EDITOR.
3. Click **EXPORT** with nothing open. You should see the "Export" header, the dashed "Drop a video here" zone, and **Recent exports** at the bottom.
4. Click **Pick from Library** and choose a recording. Export opens on it, with the thumbnail, title, ORIGINAL and the real duration, size and file size in the header. The stage shows the fox and "Where is it going?", with no card selected.
5. Press → a few times, then ←. The pink selection moves along the seven cards, and the stage shows "For …" for each one.
6. Pick **YouTube**. Switch between 1440p and 4K and check that the estimates and the "Uploaded at …" crop update. Press **Enter**. The export starts in the background, the screen stays, and the rail's EXPORT badge shows 1.
7. Pick **GitHub · Jira**. The size bar should say "fits the 10 MB limit" for a short recording, or "over GitHub's 10 MB free-plan limit" for a long one.
8. Pick **TikTok · Reels**, switch Fill / Fit, and export.
9. At the default 900×670 window, check that the page doesn't scroll. Shrink the window: the destination row scrolls sideways on its own, and the stage scrolls on its own.
10. Click **Change video** and pick another recording. Export reopens on it, keeping the selected destination.
11. Drag an MP4 from Finder anywhere onto Export. It's imported and Export opens on it.
12. Open **LIBRARY**. There's no drop strip and no Prepare or Import buttons, and dropping a file there does nothing.
13. Open a recording's page and use its "Prepare for…" or quick chips. They land on Export with that destination selected.
14. Open the old URL form `#/prepare/<assetId>?to=github`, for example from the dev tools console with `location.hash = …`. It redirects to `#/export/<assetId>?to=github`.
